title: Residue-power local conjugacy for sheet restriction of actual Weil pullback
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, m≥1, a separated finite-type k₀-scheme X₀, a prime ℓ≠p, and an algebraic closure Ω of Q_ℓ, with the actual common-stage constructible Weil hearts [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Use the actual extension model, projection, closed image and residue degree of [def-dl-a1-constant-extension-data] and [def-zl-constant-extension-restriction-local-data]. Let R be any functor from the k₀-Weil heart of the extension model to its k_m-Weil heart satisfying ConstantExtensionSheetSpec [def-zl-constant-extension-sheet-pullback-data]. For every constructible Weil sheaf F on X₀ and every closed point z of the extension model, put x=g_m(z) and f=[κ(z):κ(x)]. Then ConstantExtensionLocalConjugacy holds for F, R(g_m^*F), x, z, f: for every common finite coefficient stage, every pair of Weil presentations of these objects, and every pair of residue embeddings, the scalar-extended degree-zero stalks admit an isomorphism e with e F_z = F_x^f e. The exponent is the actual residue degree. No equivalence, exactness, residue-degree formula, or weight assertion is part of this statement.

proof.text: Regard the actual projection from X₀×k₀ k_m to X₀ as a morphism over k₀. Its residue algebra at z is literally the algebra defining constantExtensionResidueDegree. Apply the generic constructible Weil-pullback local-Frobenius comparison at geometric lifts compatible with the projection, obtaining the fth power of the operator at the image.

The sheet-return comparison identifies the local operator of the k₀-pullback with the operator of its return over k_m. Any functor satisfying ConstantExtensionSheetSpec has that return: compose its natural carrier comparison with the inverse of the comparison for the specified return functor, and lift through the displayed Weil-map equations to a natural Weil isomorphism. Compose the two local comparisons.

Choose first the embedding of the image residue field induced by the chosen embedding at z. The resulting geometric lifts are compatible. For arbitrary residue embeddings and arbitrary finite Weil presentations, apply sfLocalFrobenius_model_conjugacy at each of the two base-field data. Represent the object, the two given Weil presentations and all comparison arrows over one finite coefficient field; naturality transports the two return operators along those presentation isomorphisms. The normalized scalar-comparison equations identify the resulting maps after extension to Ω with localClosedFrobeniusCohomology in the definition of ConstantExtensionLocalConjugacy. Compose the isomorphisms in the direction from the original stalk to the restricted stalk; composition preserves the fth power. This gives the equation for every presentation and every pair of residue embeddings, including zero stalks and m=1.

lean.statement:
theorem constantExtensionRestrictionLocalConjugacy
    (R : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl (constantExtensionOriginalModel D m hm X₀) Ω ⥤
      sfCommonStageWeilSheaf (constantExtensionDatum D m hm) l hl
        (constantExtensionModel D m hm X₀) Ω)
    (hR : ConstantExtensionSheetSpec D m hm X₀ l hl Ω R)
    (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl X₀ Ω)
    (z : {z : (constantExtensionModel D m hm X₀).left //
      z ∈ closedPoints (constantExtensionModel D m hm X₀).left}) :
    ConstantExtensionLocalConjugacy D m hm X₀ l hl Ω X₀ F
      (R.obj ((zlWeilPull D l hl Ω (constantExtensionProjection D m hm X₀)).obj F))
      (constantExtensionClosedImage D m hm X₀ z) z
      (constantExtensionResidueDegree D m hm X₀ z.val)
